---
title: "Training on multiple GPUs"
---

![Common forms of parallelism during training, from @raschka2023sometechniquestomakeyourpytorchmodel.](images/forms_of_parallelism.png)

METIS can use multiple GPUs on one machine through *data parallelism*.
Identical copies of the model process different parts of a batch, then average
their gradients before updating the model. More involved forms of parallelism,
such as splitting one model across machines, are outside this interface.

## From one to four GPUs

After [setting up CUDA](../basics/installing_metis.qmd#optional-cuda-setup), our
usual single-GPU command for the bundled SIRDS bank is:

```bash
uv run metis train training.device=cuda
```

To use four GPUs on the same machine, set `training.num_devices`:

```bash
uv run metis train training.device=cuda training.num_devices=4
```

METIS starts a worker process for each GPU. Hydra configuration, output
directories, checkpoints and W&B logging use the same workflow as a single GPU.

To use only GPUs 2 and 3, restrict which devices are visible:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2,3 uv run metis train training.device=cuda training.num_devices=2
```

## Batch size

`training.batch_size` is the global batch size and must be divisible by
`training.num_devices`. For example, a batch size of 128 with four GPUs gives
each GPU 32 realisations per optimiser step.

From Python, the equivalent is
`TrainingConfig(device="cuda", num_devices=4, batch_size=128)`. Put the training
call inside `if __name__ == "__main__":` when launching multiprocessing scripts.
The installed CLI is the simpler way to launch a distributed run from a
terminal.

## Troubleshooting

- Confirm that `nvidia-smi` lists the GPUs you intend to use and that PyTorch can access CUDA.
- Check that the global batch size is divisible by the device count.
- Set `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` when diagnosing CUDA communication failures.
- Establish a successful single-GPU run before adding more devices.

The full simulation bank still needs to fit in host memory. Resuming a training
checkpoint requires the same device topology as the saved run.
